Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nora James (Findly Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Findly Principal Engineer), Priya Singh (Findly Data Scientist)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Findly through Hosted API embeddings + reranking demo. Discussed architecture for semantic search: generate embeddings for docs, ANN retrieval, then rerank with Redwood's rerank endpoint. Covered latency vs cost tradeoffs, indexing options, security (SOC 2, KMS), and next steps to run a POC benchmark on Findly data.
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching
Security and compliance (SOC 2, KMS, VPC options)
POC bench plan and next steps
transcript: 00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Samir is our SE, he'll run through the demo. Nora: Great, thanks. We got about 45-60 minutes? 00:18 Samir Patel: Cool, I'll share my screen. Quick agenda: embeddings, ANN recall, then rerank walkthrough in the Redwood Console and API, and then Q&A. 00:35 Nora: Sounds good. Quick context: Findly does candidate search, latency sensitive, about 100ms P95 target on search, and cost is a big factor - we're trying to reduce manual tuning and get better relevance. 01:05 Samir: Perfect. High-level flow: 1) call hosted embeddings endpoint to encode docs and queries, 2) index vectors in FAISS or your vector store, 3) do ANN retrieval top-K, 4) call our rerank API to score and sort. We show how Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization settings. 01:40 Liam: Quick Q — do you recommend using Pinecone or self-hosted FAISS? 01:48 Samir: Both are supported. For 100ms SLOs at our scale, many customers use a hybrid: FAISS on dedicated infra for retrieval, or Pinecone for managed. Redwood integrates either; our Console will show recall diagnostics. 02:12 Priya Singh: For rerank, is that a cross-encoder that looks at full doc text? 02:17 Samir: Yeah, the rerank endpoint runs a cross-attention model on query+candidate pairs. It expects the candidate text and will return a score; it's optimized for short candidate lists (top 10-50). Typical latency is ~60-200ms depending on model and input length, we can choose smaller rerank models to hit lower latency. 02:47 Nora: How do embeddings dimensionality and quantization affect recall? 02:53 Samir: Good question. Lower-d embeddings or aggressive 8-bit quantization can drop fine-grained recall. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload — we ran an eval on a 50k corpus that showed 1-3% nDCG loss for 8-bit in exchange for 2-3x throughput gains. 03:30 Samir: I'll demo the console — open: Console -> Models -> Hosted API -> Embeddings. 03:45 [screen share noise] 04:05 Samir: Here's the embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, input text, returns vector. We'll show a quick code sample in Python. 04:30 Samir: (reads) "from redwood import Client... client.embeddings.create(model='rw-embed-1', input=['text'])" — returns array length 1536. 04:55 Priya: Are there pre-built pipelines for indexing? 05:00 Samir: We have a reference pipeline in the docs and a sample script — link: https://redwood.ai/docs/embeddings-indexing (note: link placeholder). We'll attach the notebook. 05:25 Samir: Now the retrieval pattern: store vectors, query vector, ANN search top-100 with cosine, then rerank top-10. 05:45 Liam: Do you store embeddings in Redwood or in our infra? 05:50 Avery Chen: Hosted API stores ephemeral embeddings only; persistent index stays with you or your vector DB. For Dedicated and Private we offer tighter integrations. 06:10 Nora: Security: we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS, and audit logs. 06:18 Avery Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, supports SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations, and we can provide audit log exports and an architecture doc. We'll share our security whitepaper. 06:40 Priya: Can we run rerank inside our VPC? 06:45 Samir: For Private deployments yes; for Hosted we offer VPC peering and strict data controls, plus options for no-persist mode. 07:05 Samir: Demo time: I'll run a sample query. 07:12 [typing sounds] 07:20 Samir: Query: "senior product manager with mobile growth experience" -> embeddings -> ANN -> rerank. 07:36 Samir: Results before rerank: shows topical matches but some older profiles bubble up. 07:50 Samir: Now calling rerank endpoint with top-10 candidates. Response includes scores and explanation string. 08:08 Nora: Explanation string? 08:11 Samir: It's a short model output explaining why a doc scored higher, helpful for inspectability in POCs. It's probabilistic so treat as hint. 08:35 Priya: Do we pass embeddings to rerank or raw text? 08:39 Samir: Either pattern. We pass raw text + metadata; the rerank model recomputes cross attention so embeddings aren't required for rerank, but you can include embeddings for hybrid scoring. 09:00 Liam: Performance — how many QPS can this handle? 09:05 Samir: Depends on model size and batching. For rw-rerank-small you can get ~50 QPS on a single GPU; with batching and dedicated pool we get higher throughput. Redwood Optimize recommends batching up to X requests per 10ms window depending on SLOs. 09:30 Nora: Cost model? 09:33 Avery Chen: Hosted is usage-based. Embeddings per call + rerank per document scoring. We gave a sample cost calc in the deck; I'll send a tailored pricing sheet after this. 10:02 Samir: Walkthrough of console: per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and rerank dashboard that shows distribution of input sizes. 10:28 Samir: Now switching to API examples for rerank. 10:35 [code paste noise] 10:45 Samir: POST /v1/rerank body: {"model":"rw-rerank-1","query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"..."},...]} -> returns scores. 11:10 Priya: Is there a batch rerank endpoint? 11:14 Samir: We have both synchronous and async batch endpoints; batch is recommended for offline re-ranking. 11:28 Nora: Can we measure regression with our evals? 11:32 Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties into eval sets and will alert on quality regressions tied to model updates. 12:05 [small crosstalk] 12:20 Liam: On indexing, what about update velocity? We add 500 records per minute. 12:28 Samir: That's fine — do incremental indexing in your FAISS or use a managed store; we also support sharded indexes for high ingest. 13:00 Nora: A concern: we need <=100ms end-to-end latency; rerank + ANN might push that. 13:10 Samir: Some customers use a two-pass approach: lightweight semantic filter (embedding nearest neighbors) with fingerprinting for very low latency, and rerank only on the top 5 for interactive queries. Also tune rerank model or use smaller model for sub-100ms. 13:40 Priya: What's the best practice for feature engineering? Use metadata signals in reranker? 13:45 Samir: Yes, include structured fields in candidate payload (title, recency, score) and the reranker can consume them as text or as explicit features in the payload; our API accepts metadata that the model can incorporate. 14:10 [laptop chair noise] 14:24 Samir: Let's run a quick parallel benchmark — I will run a micro-benchmark against rw-embed-1 + rw-rerank-small with a 1k query sample. 14:40 [typing] 15:05 Samir: Running... initial P95 look like 120ms for rerank + retrieval combined in our hosted env for this sample. 15:30 Nora: That's promising. Have you run this on production-ish data distribution? 15:35 Samir: We asked for a sample corpus; if you share 5k queries and corpus we can run the POC in your infra for representative numbers. 16:00 Liam: Failure modes? 16:05 Samir: Timeout on rerank -> we fallback to ANN ranking; we also support canary rollouts so new rerank models don't go to prod until validated. 16:30 Priya: About explainability: can we get token-level reasons? 16:36 Samir: We provide short rationale summaries; token-level saliency is not exposed by default but we can run custom evals. 17:00 Avery Chen: Security follow-up — we'll attach SOC2 report and network diagrams. 17:12 Nora: Also need contract language around data retention. 17:18 Avery Chen: We'll include retention SLAs in the contract options. 17:35 Samir: Demo wrap-up — I'll paste the code snippets and the notebook link in chat. 17:48 [link posted] 18:00 Nora: Ok, some specific technical asks: 1) sample rerank config for top-10, 2) benchmark script, 3) security docs. 18:10 Avery Chen: We'll send those. 18:25 Priya: For the POC, can we test on a private cluster? 18:29 Samir: Yes - we can run a Dedicated pool or Private deployment for POC if required; typically we start on-hosted then move to Dedicated if needed. 18:55 Nora: Budget cycle is next quarter, so we'd like to run a two-week POC and ideally have numbers before budget decision. 19:05 Avery Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose dates and resource requirements. 19:25 Liam: Edge cases: multilingual search — how are embeddings handled? 19:30 Samir: Models support multilingual embeddings; sometimes you want language-specific tokenizers and models, Redwood Optimize will surface which model matches your distribution. 20:00 Priya: Any gotchas with chunking long docs? 20:05 Samir: Chunking strategy matters for rerank; you can pass longer docs but split into logical chunks and maintain doc-level aggregation. 20:32 [pause] 21:00 Samir: Quick recap of api endpoints: /v1/embeddings, /v1/search (optional), /v1/rerank, batch endpoints and async ingest. 21:20 Nora: Can you send sample cost calc with our cartridge? 21:24 Avery Chen: Yes. 21:40 [noise] 22:00 Samir: Final Qs? 22:12 Priya: How do you handle model updates and regression detection? 22:18 Samir: Redwood Optimize runs evals on your labeled sets and flags regression; we can pin model versions during rollout. 22:45 Nora: Great. 23:00 Avery Chen: Next steps recap - we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark script, and propose POC dates. 23:20 Nora: Thanks everyone. 23:30 [meeting ends]
